title: fix: cancel queued publication when making agents private
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Clears queued publication when an owner explicitly sets a prompt agent to private through `/account/agents`.
- Keeps queued publication intact for configuration-only edits; leaves proxy pricing behavior unchanged.
- Adds a real-route/D1 regression proving the agent stays private after the former publication deadline.
- Validation: 24 focused tests, Enter typecheck, and Biome pass. Regression fails on unchanged main.

Related to the adversarial review in #14622; independent fix for existing main behavior.

gist.headline: Private means private
gist.blurb: A queued publication now withers the moment an owner makes their prompt agent private. Configuration edits can keep their place in line; an explicit privacy choice gets the final word.
gist.summary: Setting a prompt agent to private via `/account/agents` now clears any queued publication, while configuration-only edits and proxy pricing behavior remain unchanged.
gist.impact: Owners can make an agent private with confidence: it will stay private after its former publication deadline instead of later becoming public from an old queue entry.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden keeper closing a small private greenhouse around a code-plant agent, while a faded queued-publication calendar page is removed from a nearby noticeboard. The scene should make the privacy setting feel deliberate and protected, with a gentle contrast between the cozy private greenhouse and the harmless cancelled queue.
